title: Article 358 — Suspension of provisions of Article 19 during emergencies

content.overview: Article 358 provides that while a Proclamation of Emergency declaring that the security of India or any part of its territory is threatened by war or by external aggression is in operation, the rights conferred by Article 19 are automatically suspended to the extent that the State may make any law or take any executive action which the State would be competent to make or take but for Article 19. The automatic suspension does not apply to a Proclamation based only on armed rebellion. Laws/actions inconsistent with Article 19 to the extent of the suspension are protected for the Emergency period; after the Proclamation ceases, such laws cease to have effect to the extent of the inconsistency except as to things done or omitted before expiry. The 44th Amendment confined automatic suspension to war/external aggression Emergencies.
content.glance: During National Emergency on war/external aggression: Art 19 rights automatically suspended for State action that would otherwise violate Art 19. Not automatic for armed-rebellion-only Emergency (44th Amendment).
content.study:
Article 358 automatic suspension of Article 19:
- Applies when Emergency is on ground of war or external aggression (not solely armed rebellion — 44th Amendment).
- State may make laws / take executive action that would otherwise violate Article 19.
- Protection for the duration; post-Emergency sunset for inconsistent laws except past acts.

Contrast Article 359 (which requires a separate Presidential order to suspend enforcement of specified rights, and can cover rights other than Article 19).

Examination: automatic vs ordered suspension; war/external aggression only for Art 358; contrast Art 359; 44th Amendment.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Automatic suspension of Art 19 during Emergency based on war or external aggression.
2. Does not apply automatically to armed-rebellion-only Emergency.
3. State may act as if Art 19 did not constrain it; post-Emergency inconsistent laws lapse prospectively.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the effect of Article 358 on Article 19?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 358, while a Proclamation of Emergency on the ground of war or external aggression is in operation, the rights conferred by Article 19 are suspended to the extent that the State may make any law or take any executive action which it would be competent to make or take but for the provisions of Article 19. This automatic suspension does not apply where the Emergency is declared only on the ground of armed rebellion. After the Proclamation ceases, inconsistent laws cease to have effect to the extent of the inconsistency, except as to things done or omitted before such cessation.

examTips: Automatic Art 19 suspension only for war/external aggression Emergency; contrast Art 359.

keyTakeaways: Art 358: automatic suspension of Art 19 during war/external-aggression Emergency.
